He is also the head coach of the [[South Sudanese national basketball team|South Sudan national team]], who he coached at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2023 World Cup]] and [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympics]]. He played college basketball for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]] before spending 10 years in the NBA. ==Early life and college== Ivey was born in [[Harlem]] in the Manhattan borough of New York City and started on the basketball team of [[Benjamin N. Cardozo High School]], leading the team to a PSAL championship.Dicker, Ron. [https://www.nytimes.com/1999/03/27/sports/high-school-basketball-new-york-state-championships-rice-cardozo-advance-class.html "High School Basketball: New York State Championships; Rice and Cardozo Advance to Class A Final"], ''[[The New York Times]]'', March 27, 1999. Accessed September 14, 2018. He attended [[Blair Academy]] for a [[post-graduate year]].[http://www.nba.com/hawks/feature/behind_the_numbers.html Behind the Numbers: Royal Ivey], [[NBA.com]]. Accessed September 14, 2018. "'In high school I wore number 12,' says Ivey, who led Cardozo HS in Queens to their first-ever New York PSAL title during his senior year before doing a post graduate year at Blair Academy in New Jersey." Ivey played [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Texas at Austin]], in which he finished as the school's all-time career leader in games started (126).[http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/RoyalIveySigns_070918.html Bucks sign Royal Ivey], September 18, 2007 ==Professional career== Ivey was selected with the 37th overall pick in the [[2004 NBA draft]] by the Atlanta Hawks. On September 18, 2007, Ivey signed a one-year contract with the Bucks. On July 24, 2008, Ivey agreed to terms with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/sixers/20080724_Sixers_reach_agreement_with_free-agent_Ivey.html |title=Sixers reach agreement with free-agent Ivey {{!}} Philadelphia Daily News {{!}} 07/24/2008 |access-date=July 25, 2008 |archive-date=December 3, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081203111829/http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/sixers/20080724_Sixers_reach_agreement_with_free-agent_Ivey.html |url-status=dead }} On June 15, 2009, Philadelphia announced that Ivey declined the player option on his contract for the 2009–10 season, making him an [[unrestricted free agent]]. However, he re-signed with the 76ers in August 2009.[http://www.philly.com/inquirer/sports/20090811_76ers_bring_back_Royal_Ivey.html 76ers bring back Royal Ivey] On February 18, 2010, Ivey was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] along with [[Primoz Brezec]] in exchange for [[Jodie Meeks]] and [[Francisco Elson]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks_sixers_100218.html |title=Bucks Acquire Ivey, Brezec from 76ers |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=February 18, 2010 |access-date=February 18, 2010}} On July 21, 2010, Ivey signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].[http://www.nba.com/2010/news/07/21/thunder.ivey.ap/index.html?rss=true Thunder sign free agent Royal Ivey] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100723112302/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/07/21/thunder.ivey.ap/index.html?rss=true |date=July 23, 2010 }} He reached the NBA Finals with the Thunder in 2012, but the team lost to the [[Miami Heat]]. On July 27, 2012, Ivey returned to the 76ers.[http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-free-agent-guard-royal-ivey Sixers Sign Free Agent Guard Royal Ivey] On September 30, 2013, he signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14381 |title=Atlanta Hawks fill up their training camp roster |access-date=October 1, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131015214846/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14381 |archive-date=October 15, 2013 |url-status=dead }} However, he was waived on October 25.{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14641 |title=Atlanta Hawks waive Royal Ivey |access-date=October 26, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029190438/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14641 |archive-date=October 29, 2013 |url-status=dead }} On January 16, 2014, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].[http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_ivey_140116 Thunder Signs Royal Ivey to 10-Day Contract] On January 26, 2014, his 10-day contract expired and the Thunder chose not to offer him a second 10-day contract.[http://newsok.com/royal-iveys-10-day-contract-with-the-thunder-expires-he-will-leave-for-china/article/3927714 Royal Ivey's 10-day contract with the Thunder expires; he will leave for China] On January 29, 2014, he signed with the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of China for rest of the 2013–14 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/110936/royal-ivey-signs-with-guangdong-southern-tigers.html Royal Ivey signs with Guangdong Southern Tigers] ==Coaching career== On September 29, 2014, Ivey was named an assistant coach for the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the [[NBA Development League]] for the 2014–15 season, effectively ending his 10-year playing career.{{Cite web |date=September 29, 2014 |title=Thunder Announces Basketball Operations Staff Promotions and Additions |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_bballops_140929 |access-date=September 29, 2014 |website=NBA.com}} On July 1, 2016, Ivey was elevated from a player development assistant with the Blue to an assistant coach with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |date=July 1, 2016 |title=Thunder Announces Coaching Staff Update |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/coachingstaff_160701 |access-date=July 1, 2016 |website=NBA.com}} On June 7, 2018, Ivey joined the [[New York Knicks]] as an assistant coach to [[David Fizdale]].{{cite web |date=June 7, 2018 |title=New York Knicks Announce Coaching Hires |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/new-york-knicks-announce-coaching-hires |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=NBA.com}} Ivey remained with the Knicks after Fizdale's firing and served under interim head coach [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1964)|Mike Miller]].{{Cite web |date=December 6, 2019 |title=Knicks Relieve David Fizdale of Head Coaching Duties |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-relieve-david-fizdale-head-coaching-duties |access-date=December 6, 2019 |website=NBA.com}}{{Cite web |date=December 6, 2019 |title=Knicks fire David Fizdale after Eastern Conference-worst 4-18 mark |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28238796/knicks-fire-david-fizdale-eastern-conference-worst-4-18-mark |access-date=December 6, 2019 |website=ESPN.com}} On November 11, 2020, the [[Brooklyn Nets]] hired Ivey as an assistant coach under [[Steve Nash]].{{cite tweet |user=BrooklynNets |number=1326618853103775747 |date=November 11, 2020 |title=OFFICIAL: We've added Royal Ivey as an assistant coach on head coach Steve Nash's staff.}}{{cite web |title=Nets add new assistant in Royal Ivey |url=https://www.netsdaily.com/2020/11/11/21561332/nets-add-another-assistant-the-knicks-royal-ivey |website=NetsDaily |access-date=November 12, 2020 |date=November 11, 2020}} On July 3, 2023, Ivey was hired by the [[Houston Rockets]] as an assistant coach.{{cite web |last1= |first1= |date=July 3, 2023 |title=Rockets Head Coach Ime Udoka Announces Coaching Staff |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-head-coach-ime-udoka-announces-coaching-staff |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} === South Sudan national team === On May 3, 2021, Ivey signed a contract to become the head coach of the [[South Sudan men's national basketball team|South Sudan national team]], representing the [[Independence of South Sudan|youngest country in the world]]. He coached the team at [[AfroBasket 2021]], the country's first major tournament.{{cite news |date=3 May 202 |title=Ivey hired to head up Senior Men at AfroBasket |url=https://ssbfed.com/ivey-hired-to-head-up-senior-men/ |access-date=May 5, 2021 |work=South Sudan Basketball Federation}} Ivey and South Sudan won the country's first AfroBasket game against [[Uganda men's national basketball team|Uganda]],{{Cite web |title=South Sudan win first-ever AfroBasket game |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/afrobasket/2021/news/south-sudan-win-firstever-afrobasket-game |access-date=2024-08-08 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} and eventually reached the quarterfinals where the team was eliminated by defending champions [[Tunisia national basketball team|Tunisia]]. Under Ivey's coaching, South Sudan qualified for their first ever World Cup in 2023 after going undefeated in first round [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Africa)|qualifying]]. They went on to earn a first ever Olympic berth at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 games]] by finishing as the best African team at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2023 World Cup]].{{Cite web |title=2023 - The year South Sudan took over African basketball |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/2023-the-year-south-sudan-took-over-african-basketball |access-date=2024-08-08 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} Ivey and South Sudan participated at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympics]], where they won their first game over [[Puerto Rico men's national basketball team|Puerto Rico]], but went on to lose to [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia]] and [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]], thus ending their campaign in the preliminary round.{{Cite web |date=2024-08-03 |title=Bogdanovic, Jokic hold off South Sudan, pull Greece to QFs |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/bogdanovic-jokic-hold-off-south-sudan-pull-greece-to-qfs |access-date=2024-08-04 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}} Despite their elimination, the team was widely praised by media and competitors for their play.{{Cite web |date=2024-07-27 |title=South Sudan's unique attire at Paris Olympics draws praise from LeBron James |url=https://english.mathrubhumi.com/special-pages/2024-paris-olympics/south-sudan-unique-attire-paris-olympics-lebron-james-1.9764142 |access-date=2024-08-08 |website=English.Mathrubhumi |language=en}} ==Personal life== Ivey is named after his grandfather, Roy Allen, who was one of the first African-American stage directors to work in television.{{cite web |last1=Abrams |first1=Jonathan |title=His Own Words: Royal Ivey |url=https://grantland.com/the-triangle/his-own-words-royal-ivey/ |website=Grantland |access-date=May 10, 2025 |date=August 25, 2011}} During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Ivey returned to the University of Texas to finish his degree in applied learning and development. He got married in 2023 to Deanna Herrington.{{cite web |url=http://alcalde.texasexes.org/2011/12/texas-ex-royal-ivey-uses-nba-lockout-to-finish-degree|title=Texas Ex Royal Ivey Uses NBA Lockout to
